To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a topic model can be used to represent a sequence of observations from RGB-D sensor readings, (2) a temporal topic model can be extended to represent temporal relations, and (3) an object topic model can be applied to represent object relations.

(1) a new representation for RGB-D sensor readings is proposed that is suitable for LDA; (2) a novel topic model is introduced that takes into account the temporal information of the observed actions; (3) a novel topic is introduced that takes the object relational information into the observed actions; and (4) the proposed models are validated using a real robot in a simulated environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can a robot recognize what an agent in the environment is doing, given the robot’s observations of the environment and knowledge about the world?
how to use topic models to recognize the plans of people in real time, and how to use this information for robot planning and action selection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temporal and relational extensions of topic models are useful for the purpose of plan and activity recognition in real-time HRI.
the proposed methods are effective and robust for plan and activity recognition.

our approach can be used to recognize both the temporal and relational structure of a person's actions in real time and with a high degree of accuracy, even when the person is wearing a mask and the robot is unable to see their face.

we propose a novel approach to the problem of plan and activity recognition using topic models and we show that temporal and object relations can be incorporated into these models.
